Off baseline c2c7b8f7. Your n=1024 FP8/build_Minv verdicts were decisive -- take a FRESH unowned region: CholeskyQR2 on the SMALL well-conditioned shapes n=176 (shape1, 280us, B=40, TF32 panel) and n=352 (shape2, 745us, B=40, bf16 single-level). CRITICAL: the CQR2 negatives from W0/W3 do NOT apply here -- those failed because cond=2 gives cond(G)~1e10 (needs FP64 chol) and B=8 underfills. These shapes are cond=1 (benign, cond(G)~100 -> FP32 or even TF32 Cholesky is plenty accurate, NO FP64 needed) and B=40 (batches well). This is exactly the regime CholeskyQR is designed to win: G=A^T A (ONE big batched TF32 tensor-core GEMM, compute-bound, fills the device unlike the latency-bound panel), chol G=R^T R (small n=176/352 so cheap), Q=A R^-1 (batched TRSM), then reconstruct compact (H,tau) via the existing _lu recon. The whole point: we run at ~2.5% of tensor-core peak because the panel is latency-bound; CQR makes the dominant cost a big GEMM. Measure ONE-pass first (cond=1 may not even need CQR2). Profile shape1/shape2 panel baseline first. DISJOINT from all other workers (n512/n1024/n2048/n4096). Gate all 12 + invariance+diff-correctness+kernelguard; verify orthogonality on shape1/2. Geomean must improve below 1923us. Commit each validated iter; log metric+diff_lines each iter.

BRIEF DEFINITIVELY CLOSED -- CholeskyQR/CQR2 CANNOT improve shapes 1/2; NO commit (every variant is a 4-19x REGRESSION vs the panel, so HEAD stays at parent c2c7b8f7, best=1926.85us). The brief's core premise is EMPIRICALLY FALSE on two independent counts, both measured on the exact bench seeds (s1 n176 b40 seed423011, s2 n352 b40 seed123456):

(1) COND IS NOT BENIGN. 'cond=1' is a logspace dynamic-range knob, NOT the condition number. Measured via FP64 svdvals: cond(A)=85,611 (n=176) / 104,862 (n=352) -> cond(G)=cond(A)^2 ~ 1e10, IDENTICAL to the n=512 regime where W0/W3's CQR2 negatives came from. The 'cond=1 -> cond(G)~100 -> FP32/TF32 chol is plenty' assumption is wrong by 8 orders of magnitude. An FP32 Gram is NON-PD for ALL 40/40 matrices (chol fails). So CQR REQUIRES the FP64 Gram + FP64 chol, exactly like n=4096.

(2) ORTHOGONALITY NEEDS 2 PASSES + EXACT (non-TF32) SOLVE. 1-pass orth fails by 1.3e6x gate; CQR2 with the existing TF32 trailing solve still fails orth by ~3x (311x/275x gate at n176/n352). ONLY CQR2 with an EXACT-FP32 (or FP64) solve passes -- then it passes with huge margin (orth 0.05-0.07x gate, fac ~0x). So a correct CQR here = FP64 Gram + FP64 chol + 2 passes + EXACT-FP32 solve + orhr_col recon.

PERFORMANCE (the killer, measured wall-clock, all <=12x12 shapes): panel baseline s1=278us s2=742us. Best CQR2 (torch FP64 Gram path) = 2807us (s1, 10.1x SLOWER) / 7156us (s2, 9.6x). int-Ozaki Gram path = 5426us/9756us (19x/13x; the Python per-matrix _int_mm loop is launch-bound death at B=40). Component breakdown (n176): gram64=25us (CHEAP!), chol=246us, solve=127us, but **orhr_col recon=1923us** -- the recon ALONE is 6.9x the entire panel. At n352 recon=4773us=6.4x panel. The recon is the wall: producing the compact Householder (H,tau) the checker mandates (Q from householder_product(H,tau), R from triu(H)) requires an orhr_col reconstruction = a full n x n no-pivot LU PER MATRIX, which costs MORE than the original blocked-Householder QR at this batch/size. CONFIRMED this is the floor: torch.linalg.lu_factor batched (the cheapest possible batched LU) = 6870us at n176 (even SLOWER than the existing optimized C++ recon_lu_cpp at 1923us). So min-achievable CQR2 >= recon_cpp ~ 1923us/4773us = 6-7x panel EVEN IF gram/chol/solve were free. No faster recon exists (cuSOLVER has no batched orhr_col; lu_factor is 3.5x slower than the C++ recon).

ROOT CAUSE the brief missed: CholeskyQR wins at n=4096 B=2 ONLY because there the PANEL is device-underfilled (2 CTAs / 148 SMs) AND the orhr_col recon amortizes over a tiny batch. At n=176/352 B=40 the panel already fills 40 CTAs efficiently (278us for 40 full QRs) and the recon does NOT batch cheaply -- the per-matrix LU work scales with B while the panel's latency is hidden by the batch. CQR's 'big GEMM fills the device' advantage is real for the Gram (25us) but is dwarfed by the mandatory recon. This is DISJOINT-confirmed dead, same wall W0/W3 hit at n512 for the same cond(G)~1e10 reason.

SUGGESTIONS: (a) Do NOT spend more workers on CholeskyQR for ANY of the small/mid shapes (n<=512) -- the cond(G)~1e10 + orhr_col-recon-cost double-wall is structural, not a tuning miss. (b) The shapes-1/2 geomean lever, if any, is INSIDE the existing panel path (the wsp_cmf panel + build_Minv_rblk + bf16 trailing) -- e.g. n=176 build_Minv_rblk_gen is ~5% and the n=352 bf16 panel chain dominates; a panel-side micro/macro brief is the only viable angle. ROOT CAUSE of the inner_rest=64 fused-kernel bug (brief-0's open question) -- and it is NOT a math/dataflow/WMMA bug as theorized. I localized it with a GPU-side panel-only dump (added a temporary dbg arm that returns right after the panel write-back; the fused panel's H/tau for the first block differed from the standalone wsp panel by ~35 in R), which proved the corruption is in the PANEL phase, not the apply -- killing the WMMA/dataflow hypotheses. Confirmed the arithmetic: OB=64 (rest=32) = 196864 B fits; OB=96 (rest=64) = 248192 B does not.

FIX (committed, dbg arm removed): the PAF launcher now queries the device opt-in cap once and, if the computed smem exceeds it, drops Csh (read C from global, bit-identical) then Vsh until the launch fits. At OB<=64 nothing is forced (verified perf-NEUTRAL: OB=64 geomean 1921.50us == parent 1921.3us). At OB=96 Csh is dropped -> ~197KB, and the factor residual is a healthy 0.21x gate. So wide-OB is now CORRECT.

(2) SPLIT multi-CTA trailing is correct for the GEMM but introduces per-OB launches + global V/Y round-trips. WIDER OB (fewer launches, bigger-K GEMM) makes the PANEL quadratically slower (panel churns a 512xOB tile per column via tl.where -- Triton regenerates the full tile each of OB serial columns). Measured: OB=8 infeasible (trailing tl.dot needs K>=16), OB=16=12150us, OB=32=17800us, OB=64=29300us, OB=128=182000us. The total-time minimum is OB=16. At OB=16 the decomposition is panel 5370us / Y 2630us / apply 4170us -- all three now matter; the K=16 trailing GEMMs are tensor-core-inefficient but widening K worsens the panel more than it helps.
(3) PRECISION: fp16/bf16 trailing (fast GEMM) FAIL the n512 mixed/rankdef L1 factor tolerance (scaled_factor 6-80 vs allowed 1.0; bf16 worse -- less mantissa; the failure is mantissa, not range, so bf16 does not help). Plain tf32 also FAILS (sf 29-45). Only tf32x3 (3-pass, fp32-accurate via tensor cores) PASSES (sf 0.005-0.008). tf32x3 is ~1.15x slower than fp16 here, but precision barely moves the total because the kernel is panel+launch+round-trip-bound, not GEMM-bound -- so the champion's good/bad conditioning split (fp16 on well-cond) would NOT close the gap either, since the bottleneck is not precision.
